title: Brain Detective
sub: Looking Closer at What We See · Grades 1–2 · 25 minutes · General / Homeroom
objective: Students will learn that their brains make predictions about what they see, and will practice the skill of checking their assumptions before deciding.
materials: Paper with scrambled sentence: “I cna raed tihs eevn wehn its msesed up”
Two pictures that look similar but have small differences
**Recommended from Perception Lab:** Rubin’s Vase (#4 — faces or vase?), Balcony (#3 — bistable figure)
connection: **Option 1 — Visit:** Students use a stereoscope that makes flat pictures look 3D, and see cards that change when you move them—fun tricks just like today’s optical illusions!

steps.title: Can you read this?
script: Write the scrambled sentence on the board:
*“Can you read this even though the letters are mixed up? Raise your hand if you could read it!”* (Most students will be able to.)

screen.question: I cna raed tihs eevn wehn its msesed up

steps.purpose: Show the class that their brains read what the letters only suggest.
students: Can you read this even though the letters are mixed up?
Raise your hand if you could read it!

steps.title: How did you do that?
script: *“How did you do that? Your brain is so smart that it predicts what words should be there. It knows what makes sense, so it fills in the blanks. But sometimes our brains predict wrong things too!”*
steps.purpose: Name what happened: the brain predicts, and sometimes it predicts wrong.
students: Your brain is so smart that it predicts what words should be there.

steps.title: Picture Detective
script: Show the old woman/young woman illusion (or vase/faces): *“What do you see?”*
Let students share their first impressions

screen.alt: Rubin’s Vase: a white vase on black, or two dark faces looking at each other
screen.caption: Rubin’s Vase

steps.purpose: First impressions: every child says what they see.

steps.title: A different way
script: Guide them to see the alternate interpretation: *“Can anyone see it a different way?”*
*“Your eyes are looking at the same picture, but your brain can see it two different ways! This is called an optical illusion.”*

items.label: A vase
items.alt: Rubin’s Vase with the vase picked out

items.label: Two faces
items.alt: Rubin’s Vase with the two faces picked out

steps.purpose: Find the second reading: the same picture, two ways to see it.
students: Can anyone see it a different way?

steps.title: Spot the Difference
script: Show two similar pictures with subtle differences
*“At first glance, do these look the same or different?”* (Most will say same)

screen.question: At first glance, do these look the same or different?

steps.purpose: A quick first look, before any checking.

steps.title: Look closer
script: *“Now let’s be Brain Detectives and look closer…”*
Students identify differences
*“See? Sometimes we need to look closer before we decide what we’re seeing!”*

screen.question: Now let’s be Brain Detectives and look closer…

steps.purpose: Students find the differences, and see why it pays to look again.
students: Sometimes we need to look closer before we decide what we’re seeing!

steps.title: Think about real life
script: *“Let’s think about real life. Has anyone ever thought someone took their pencil, but it was actually just in their desk? Or thought a friend was ignoring them, but they just didn’t hear?”*

screen.question: Has anyone ever thought someone took their pencil, but it was actually just in their desk? Or thought a friend was ignoring them, but they just didn’t hear?

steps.purpose: Bring the Brain Detective habit from pictures into everyday life.

steps.title: Before I Decide, I Will…
script: Create a class chart on chart paper: **“Before I Decide, I Will…”**
Look closer
Ask questions
Check if I have all the information
Remember my brain might be making a prediction
Let students contribute their own ideas. Hang the chart in the classroom as a reminder.
steps.purpose: Build the class chart together; children add their own ideas.
students: Check if I have all the information
Remember my brain might be making a prediction

steps.title: This week, be a Brain Detective!
script: *“This week, be a Brain Detective! When you think you know what you’re seeing, pause and look closer first. Sometimes our brains make guesses that aren’t quite right.”*

screen.question: This week, be a Brain Detective!

steps.purpose: Send the class off with one habit to practice this week.
students: When you think you know what you’re seeing, pause and look closer first.
